reason: The cited evidence confirms increased atomic size difference with Zr (E4), a single BCC phase after processing (E1), excellent room-temperature strength and ductility (E1, E2), and low density ~5 g/cm³ (E1). However, none of the cited passages report high-temperature mechanical testing or a 20% yield strength improvement at ~800 °C, so the key premise of high-temperature strengthening is unsupported.
premises: Zr addition increases atomic size difference and lattice distortion in Ti65(AlCrNbV)-based alloys
A single-phase BCC structure can be maintained with ~7 at.% Zr after thermomechanical processing
Solid solution strengthening from Zr improves high-temperature yield strength by ~20%
Room-temperature ductility is preserved after Zr addition and processing
Alloy density remains ~5 g/cm³ with Zr addition
